prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in League City, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1353; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Understood. Where were you living at the time of the collision?
A: In League City, Texas, in a townhome off the main road near the freeway.

Q: Let's talk about the day of the accident. Where were you driving from?
A: I was coming back from a client meeting. I was in the right lane on the access road, heading toward the interchange.

Q: What happened as you approached the interchange?
A: I was about to merge onto the highway and I checked my mirror. The car in the lane to my left was moving over, and I saw it drifting toward me. I tried to move away but the side of their car hit my rear passenger door and my front fender.

Q: Did you see the other driver signal before changing lanes?
A: I don't recall a signal. I remember the car just came over into my space.

Q: After the impact, what do you remember?
A: My car spun a little and I hit the curb. My head snapped against the window frame. I remember feeling dizzy and nauseous, and the sound around me seemed far away.

Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
A: I don't think I fully blacked out, but I was confused for a while. A bystander asked me questions and I had trouble answering them.

Q: Who did you see first for medical care?
A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've seen my primary care doctor and a neurologist. I was told to rest in a dark room for several days and avoid screens. I've also had physical therapy for my neck and some vision exercises.

Q: How has your daily life changed since the accident?
A: Pretty significantly. I used to run three mornings a week. Now I get headaches if I read for more than a few minutes, and bright lights bother me. I had to step back from work for a while and I've been more irritable with my family.

Q: Are you still experiencing those symptoms today?
A: Some of them, yes. The headaches are better than they were, but they still come on in the afternoon, and I don't always trust my concentration when I'm driving.
